cards.text: Paul, the apostle who wrote this letter to the churches of Galatia (Galatians 1:1-2), has been pleading with his friends there (Galatians 4:12-20). Some of them want to be under the law. So Paul stops and asks them a question, and friend, it's the kind of question your boss asks when he KNOWS you didn't read the email.

cards.question: Paul has a question for the Galatians who want to be under the law. What does he ask them?

answers.text: Do you not understand what the law says
Have you kept every part of the law
Who was the first to teach you the law

cards.text: Then Paul goes right to what's written. Abraham, the man God promised to bless (Genesis 12:1-3), had two sons, and friend, I raised SIX on one kitchen counter, so trust me, two is where it gets interesting.

cards.question: Paul says both of Abraham's sons were born to free women.

cards.text: Paul says Abraham's two sons were born two very different ways. One came the plain old human way, like a regular batch from regular dough.

The other came because God promised it: God told Abraham his wife Sarah would bear him a son named Isaac, and Sarah, in her old age, laughed to herself at the idea (Genesis 17:19; 18:11-12). And friend, I get it, because I once asked an angel if he had the right DRAWER.

cards.question: Abraham's son by the slave woman was born according to the ___, but his son by the free woman was born through the ___.

cards.text: Now Paul says these things serve as illustrations: the two women represent two covenants. Buttercup would LOVE this guy, because he's explaining the big stuff with something you can see.

cards.question: Paul says one of the two covenants bears children into slavery. Which mountain does that covenant come from?
Paul says the covenant from Mount Sinai, the one that bears children into slavery, is ___.

cards.text: Hagar was Sarah's Egyptian servant who bore Abraham a son (Genesis 16:1, 15), and Paul says she stands for Mount Sinai in Arabia AND corresponds to the present-day Jerusalem. A mountain AND a city, friend, and the most I ever stood for was a cookie.

cards.question: Why does Paul say Hagar corresponds to the present-day Jerusalem?

answers.text: She is in slavery with her children
She was buried outside its walls
She once lived inside its gates

cards.text: Paul has just tied Hagar to the present-day Jerusalem. Then he says there's ANOTHER Jerusalem, the Jerusalem above, and friend, I can't even keep track of two oven mitts.

cards.question: Paul says the Jerusalem above is in slavery, just like the present-day Jerusalem.

cards.text: Paul says the Jerusalem above is free, and she is our mother. Then, like a guy who brings a printout to win the argument, he backs it up with words from the prophet Isaiah (Isaiah 54:1), telling a barren woman who has never had children to rejoice and cry aloud.

cards.question: The words Paul quotes tell the barren woman to rejoice. What reason do they give her?

answers.text: She will have more children than the married woman
Her husband will soon come home to her
Her fields will soon grow fruitful again

cards.text: Now Paul quits talking about Genesis and Isaiah and turns straight to the Galatians. It's like the meeting where the boss finishes the slides, spins around and goes, 'So... about YOU.'

cards.question: Paul tells the Galatian believers that, like ___, they are children of promise.

cards.text: Isaac, the promised son, did come: Sarah bore him to Abraham (Genesis 21:2-3). Then Paul goes back one more time to how things went between Abraham's two sons, like a guy rewinding the game tape to show you the play AGAIN.

cards.question: Paul says that back then, the son born by the flesh did something to the son born by the Spirit. What did he do?
Paul says that trouble between the son born by the flesh and the son born by the Spirit stayed in the past, and it's different now.

cards.text: Paul asks, 'But what does the Scripture say?' and friend, when Paul asks THAT, you put your phone down. Then he quotes it: 'Expel the slave woman and her son.'

cards.question: The Scripture Paul quotes says to expel the slave woman and her son. What reason does it give?

answers.text: Her son will never share in the inheritance
Her son broke the rules of the household
Her son was old enough to live on his own

cards.question: Paul ends by telling the believers that they are children of the slave woman.

findings.problem: Cards 5 and 6 give away both blanks. Card 6 says the other son 'came because God promised it', which hands over 'promise' word for word. Card 5's 'the plain old human way' points straight to 'flesh'. The blank no longer tests anything the baker reasons out.

rule.text: No card ever gives away the answer to a choice card that comes later.

findings.problem: The joke doesn't follow. Papa Dorin says he raised SIX, then says 'two is where it gets interesting.' That doesn't fit having handled six, so the comparison makes a reader stop and say 'huh?' instead of clicking right away.

rule.text: If a stranger would say "huh?", rewrite it.

findings.problem: The wrong answer 'Her son broke the rules of the household' can be argued as right. Gal 4:29 has just said the son born by the flesh persecuted the son born by the Spirit, so a baker could fairly say that was the reason he was sent away.

rule.text: No near-matches. A wrong answer never means the same as the right answer, or close to it. If a baker could argue it's right, replace it.
